Image caption, The statue of Sir Billy Boston in Believe Square, Wigan, was unveiled in 2016 Rehman said: "Following his passing, we wanted to ensure his legacy continues to be honoured in the heart of our town. "That's why we are renaming Believe Square, the home of Sir Billy's statue, as Sir Billy Boston Square." title: Rail users back £1bn TransPennine train plan

input.lead: Rail users react to £1bn TransPennine train plan as watchdog welcomes investment
input.summary: Rail users react to £1bn TransPennine train plan as watchdog welcomes investment
input.evidence_text: Railway passengers have said a £1bn investment in new battery-electric trains is needed to improve journeys across the TransPennine network Plans for 29 new trains have been unveiled as part of the TransPennine Route Upgrade (TRU), with the fleet expected to provide more seats for passengers travelling across the North The trains are expected to become Britain's first mainline battery-electric fleet and form part of wider TRU improvements including an electrified railway between Manchester and York, additional services and upgraded stations TRU said the changes would mean "thousands of passengers will benefit from faster, more frequent trains with more seats" Chris Jackson, Managing Director at TransPennine Express, said: "Our customers will benefit from more seats and better accessibility, including level boarding "Britain has a proud railway heritage, and this project puts the UK at the forefront of the next generation of cleaner rail technology."

title: Council to fund restoration of cleared Levenshulme alley garden

input.summary: Manchester Council blames "failures in communication" after workers rip out a community garden
input.evidence_text: A council has said it will fund a new community alley garden after workers ripped it out by mistake Manchester City Council apologised and said contractors had been responding to a report of overgrown vegetation, but instead had destroyed the intentional planting, trellises and wildlife habitats in the passageway It blamed an "inexcusable breakdown in communication and on-site judgement" for the clearance Tom Marrett, who helped establish the original garden in the Levenshulme area of Manchester, said it was a "relief" the mistake had been acknowledged, and while "you can't build a garden overnight" he hoped more people from the community would get involved in the restoration Redgate, which holds the council's passageway-cleansing contract, confirmed it was involved in the work and said it had spoken to residents about reviving the garden Marrett said residents hoped to buy mature plants and trees to accelerate the restoration, while increased interest from neighbours could allow more people to become involved

Illustration by Jake Greenhalgh ‘If it’s just a million pound, I can write a cheque to keep it going’ The parents at Alderley Edge School for Girls keep comparing their lives to a Netflix drama. “It’s like a Netflix Drama,” says Mike Ward, whose daughter started at the school just last September. Or, “it could be a Netflix special,” Adam Gough – whose daughter until recently attended the school’s nursery – tells me. So what would be the opening scene? It’s sports day here at AESG — a fee-paying institution that until last June sat on five-and-a-half acres in the leafiest bit of Cheshire, charged over £6k per pupil per term, and boasted results in the top 3% in the country. title: Asru's remains have disappeared from public display. Was this the right move?

input.summary: Join us to discuss one of Manchester Museum’s most controversial decisions
input.evidence_text: Join us to discuss one of Manchester Museum’s most controversial decisions 200 years ago, the mummified remains of a woman named Asru were unwrapped in Manchester. She had lived and died in Ancient Egypt 2,500 years before. Her coffin shows her to be a woman of status, and she died when she was around 50 to 60 years old Her body, in an open coffin, has been on almost continuous public display at Manchester Museum for two centuries. Millions know the museum as simply “the one with the mummies” But this morning the museum made a bombshell announcement: it’s taking her off display. The decision comes after a year-long public consultation, and is based on the museum’s understanding of what Asru’s wishes would have been Was this the right decision? Should we still be gazing at human remains, or is it time to leave that practice behind? And, while Asru waits in storage, what should happen to her next? All of this will be the topic of The Mill’s next big event on 24th September at Manchester Museum . Expect disagreement and impassioned debate from the expert panel and audience

Fly-tipping continues to place a significant burden on council resources, drain public money away from essential services and impact the h In 2025-26, Manchester recorded 17,954 fly-tipping incidents, resulting in the removal of more than 5,594 tonnes of waste from across the city. title: Expanding ‘trainer flat' scheme helps care leavers to thrive in adulthood - Rochdale Borough Council

input.lead: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council
input.summary: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council
input.evidence_text: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council Living alone for the first time can be a daunting experience, but it can be an even greater challenge for those who have grown up in care as some may only have a limited support network that they can rely on This can make adjusting to new responsibilities such as paying utility bills, managing a tenancy agreement, budgeting and keeping on top of household chores harder However, through the help of the local authority’s trainer flat scheme, of which there are now 14 across the borough, cared for young people aged 17 and over are being offered the perfect stepping stone to safely prepare for life on their own Fully furnished and equipped with everyday household goods, these flats provide young people with the time and support they need to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to successfully transition into adulthood This support is offered without the financial pressures normally associated with setting up a home, with the young people not required to contribute towards gas, electricity, water and other property-related utility costs until they turn 18

Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. input.evidence_text: Works will soon begin to ensure the preservation and protection of one of Manchester city centre’s most recognised landmarks For nearly four decades, the iconic Chinatown archway has stood as the gateway to the city’s famous Chinatown.
